source_reviews.independent_solution: Reused unchanged from SOURCE-FIRST and the independently frozen original view stage; no source or 117 mathematics replay. On arbitrary a>0, the principal root is rational iff a is the square of a positive rational, equivalently a=(m/n)^2 with positive integers m,n. For reduced positive rational u/v this requires both u and v to be square integers. Positive irrational a always has an irrational root, but rational a may also have an irrational root; positive integer squares alone are not the full domain criterion. The original independent source solution supplied five distinct examples per branch, including noninteger rational squares and an irrational radicand. Author source_solution states the same full criterion, excludes zero/negative inputs and correctly supplies the already reviewed examples 3,7,11/4 for irrational roots and 1/4,9/16,25/9 for rational roots. Its extra positive irrational example sqrt(3) fits the retained irrational-radicand implication.
